steps.step: Pat the pork tenderloin dry and season all over with salt and pepper.
Rub the tenderloin with the olive oil, curl the thin tail end underneath itself so it cooks at an even thickness, and set it in the air fryer basket.
Air fry at 380°F until lightly browned on the outside, about 10 minutes.
Meanwhile, whisk the honey, dijon mustard, garlic, and apple cider vinegar together in a small bowl to make the glaze.
Brush the tenderloin with half the glaze, flip it, and air fry 5 more minutes — in the tight space of a basket the glaze can catch fast, so keep an eye on it.
Brush with the remaining glaze and continue air frying until a thermometer in the thickest part reads 145°F, about 6 to 8 minutes more.
Move the tenderloin to a cutting board and let it rest 5 minutes before slicing so the juices redistribute.
Pat the pork tenderloin dry and season all over with salt and pepper.
Rub it all over with the olive oil, then preheat the grill to medium-high and set up two zones — direct heat on one side, a cooler indirect area on the other.
Sear the tenderloin directly over the hot side, turning every couple of minutes, until browned on all sides, about 8 minutes total.
While it sears, whisk the honey, dijon mustard, garlic, and apple cider vinegar together in a small bowl to make the glaze.
Move the tenderloin to the cooler side of the grill, brush with half the glaze, and close the lid.

Grill with the lid closed, brushing with the remaining glaze once or twice, until a thermometer in the thickest part reads 145°F, about 12 to 15 minutes — indirect heat lets the glaze caramelize without scorching.
Transfer to a cutting board, tent loosely with foil, and rest 5 minutes before slicing.
Heat the oven to 425°F and set a sheet pan nearby.
Pat the pork tenderloin dry, season all over with salt and pepper, and rub with the olive oil.
Set the tenderloin on the sheet pan and roast for 15 minutes to start building color, since a sheet pan won't sear the meat the way a hot skillet does.
Meanwhile, whisk the honey, dijon mustard, garlic, and apple cider vinegar together in a small bowl to make the glaze.
Brush the tenderloin with half the glaze and return the sheet pan to the oven for 8 minutes.
Brush with the remaining glaze and roast until a thermometer in the thickest part reads 145°F, about 5 to 7 minutes more.
Let the tenderloin rest on the sheet pan for 5 minutes before slicing, spooning any pan juices back over the top.
Pat the salmon fillets dry and season with salt and pepper.
Melt the butter and stir in the lemon juice, garlic, and dried dill.
Preheat the air fryer to 380°F for a few minutes — starting hot gives the fillets a bit of color they'd otherwise miss without a broiler.
Brush the salmon all over with the butter mixture and set the fillets skin-side down in the air fryer basket, leaving space between them.
Lay the lemon slices over the top of the fillets.
Air fry until the salmon flakes easily and looks opaque in the center, about 8 to 10 minutes — no need to flip.
Let the fillets rest a couple of minutes, then drizzle with any butter mixture left in the bowl before serving.
Pat the salmon fillets dry and season with salt and pepper.
Melt the butter and stir in the lemon juice, garlic, and dried dill.
Preheat the grill to medium and oil the grates well — skinless fillets stick easily, so don't skip this.
Lay the lemon slices in a row on the grates and set the salmon on top of them skin-side down; the lemon keeps the delicate fish from falling through or sticking.
Brush the fillets with the butter mixture, close the lid, and grill until the salmon flakes easily and is opaque throughout, about 8 to 10 minutes — resist flipping it.
Lift the fillets off, lemon slices and all, using a wide spatula.
Drizzle with any remaining butter mixture before serving.
Bring a large pot of salted water to a boil and cook the linguine until just short of tender, about 1 minute less than the package says. Scoop out a cup of the pasta water before draining.
Toss the shrimp with the olive oil, salt, and pepper, then thread them onto skewers.
Preheat the grill to medium-high and oil the grates.
Grill the shrimp skewers until pink, curled, and lightly charred, about 2 minutes per side.
Meanwhile, melt half the butter in a small skillet over medium heat, add the garlic and red pepper flakes, and stir until fragrant, about 30 seconds.
Pour in the white wine and let it bubble for a minute to cook off the sharp smell.
Stir in the remaining butter and the lemon juice until the sauce looks glossy.
Slide the shrimp off the skewers into the skillet, add the drained linguine, and toss well, splashing in reserved pasta water a little at a time until the sauce coats the noodles.
Scatter the parsley over the top and serve right away while the sauce is still glossy.
Toss the cabbage with the mayonnaise and half the lime juice in a bowl, season with salt, and set aside so it softens while you cook the fish.
Preheat the air fryer to 400°F.
Pat the fish dry and rub both sides with the olive oil, chili powder, cumin, salt, and pepper.
Set the fish in the air fryer basket in a single layer and air fry until it flakes easily and the edges are golden, about 8 minutes, flipping halfway.
Move the fish to a plate and break it into large flaky chunks with a fork.
Stack the tortillas, wrap loosely in foil, and warm them in the air fryer for a couple of minutes while the fish rests.
Fill each tortilla with fish and a spoonful of the cabbage slaw.
Top with cilantro and a squeeze of the remaining lime juice before serving.
Toss the cabbage with the mayonnaise and half the lime juice in a bowl, season with salt, and set aside so it softens while you cook the fish.
Preheat the grill to medium-high and oil the grates well — white fish is delicate and sticks fast.
Pat the fish dry and rub both sides with the olive oil, chili powder, cumin, salt, and pepper.
Grill the fish until it releases easily and flakes apart, with good char marks, about 3 to 4 minutes per side.
Move the fish to a plate and break it into large flaky chunks with a fork.
Warm the tortillas directly on the grill grates, about 15 to 20 seconds per side, until soft and lightly charred.
Fill each tortilla with fish and a spoonful of the cabbage slaw.
Top with cilantro and a squeeze of the remaining lime juice before serving.
Melt the butter in a small saucepan on the stovetop, whisk in the flour, and cook for 1 minute until it smells toasty, not raw.
Slowly whisk in the milk until smooth, then pour the mixture into the slow cooker.
Add the uncooked pasta, half the cheddar cheese, and salt and pepper to the slow cooker and stir to coat the pasta in the sauce.
Cover and cook on low until the pasta is tender, about 2 1/2 hours, stirring once around the halfway mark so it doesn't clump or stick to the bottom.
Stir in the tuna and frozen peas during the last 20 minutes of cooking, so they heat through without turning rubbery or falling apart.
Stir in the remaining cheddar cheese until melted.
Meanwhile, toast the breadcrumbs in a dry skillet over medium heat until golden, about 3 minutes, stirring often — this gives you a crunchy topping a slow cooker can't.
Scatter the toasted breadcrumbs over each portion just before serving so they stay crisp.
Soak the cut potatoes in a bowl of cold water for at least 15 minutes to rinse away extra starch, then drain and pat completely dry.
Toss the dried potatoes with 1 tablespoon of the vegetable oil and a pinch of salt.

Preheat the air fryer to 380°F, then air fry the potatoes in a single layer, shaking the basket every 5 minutes, until golden and crisp, about 18 to 20 minutes. Move them to a bowl and raise the temperature to 400°F.
Whisk the remaining flour, the cornstarch, the baking powder, and a pinch of salt and pepper together in a bowl for the dry coating.

Pat the fish dry, dip each piece briefly in the cold sparkling water, then press it into the dry coating until evenly covered, patting off the excess — the fizzy water helps the coating cling without needing a deep-fry batter.
Lightly brush or spray both sides of the coated fish with vegetable oil and set the pieces in the air fryer basket in a single layer.
Air fry at 400°F, flipping once halfway, until deep golden and the fish flakes easily, about 10 to 12 minutes total.
Return the potatoes to the basket for the last 2 minutes just to re-crisp and warm through.
Serve the fish and chips hot with malt vinegar on the side.
Whisk the soy sauce, honey, and cornstarch together in a small bowl until smooth and set aside.
Toss the broccoli, bell pepper, and carrot with half the vegetable oil.
Preheat the air fryer to 400°F, then air fry the vegetables in the basket, shaking once, until bright and just tender-crisp, about 8 minutes. Move them to a bowl.
Toss the shrimp with the remaining vegetable oil, garlic, and ginger.
Set the shrimp in the basket in a single layer and air fry until pink and curled, about 6 minutes, shaking halfway.
Meanwhile, warm the sauce in a small saucepan on the stovetop until it thickens and turns glossy, about 1 minute — the air fryer can't reduce a sauce for you.
Toss the air-fried vegetables and shrimp with the warm sauce until everything is coated, then serve hot.
Whisk the soy sauce, honey, and cornstarch together in a small bowl until smooth and set aside.
Thread the shrimp onto skewers. Toss the broccoli, bell pepper, and carrot with half the vegetable oil and load them into a grill basket.
Preheat the grill to medium-high and oil the grates.
Grill the vegetables in the grill basket, tossing occasionally, until charred at the edges and just tender-crisp, about 7 minutes.
Brush the shrimp skewers with the remaining vegetable oil, then grill until pink, curled, and lightly charred, about 2 minutes per side.
Meanwhile, add the garlic and ginger to a small saucepan with the sauce and simmer over medium heat, stirring, until fragrant and thickened, about 2 minutes.
Slide the shrimp off the skewers, toss everything with the grilled vegetables and warm sauce, and serve hot.
Stir the tuna, mayonnaise, and celery together in a bowl, then season with salt and pepper.
Lay out the bread slices and spread the tuna mixture evenly over two of them.
Top the tuna with the cheddar cheese, then close each sandwich with the remaining bread.
Butter the outside of each sandwich on both sides.
Preheat the griddle over medium heat — its flat, wide surface heats more evenly edge to edge than a skillet, so both sandwiches toast at the same rate.
Set the sandwiches on the griddle and cook until golden and crisp on the first side, about 3 minutes.
Flip carefully and cook the second side until golden and the cheese has melted through, about 3 more minutes.
Slice in half and serve while the cheese is still warm and stretchy.
Cook the white rice according to the package directions and keep it warm.
Whisk the tamari, honey, rice vinegar, and sesame oil together in a small bowl.
Preheat the air fryer to 380°F.
Pat the salmon dry, brush with half the sauce, and set it skin-side down in the air fryer basket.
Air fry until the fish flakes easily and looks opaque in the center, about 8 minutes, brushing with a little more sauce halfway through for a sticky glaze.
Break the salmon into large chunks.
Divide the warm rice between two bowls and top with the salmon, cucumber, and avocado.
Drizzle the remaining sauce over the bowls and finish with a scatter of sesame seeds.
Cook the white rice according to the package directions and keep it warm.
Whisk the tamari, honey, rice vinegar, and sesame oil together in a small bowl.
Preheat the grill to medium-high and oil the grates well — skinless salmon sticks fast without it.
Brush the salmon with a little of the sesame oil and set it on the hot grates. Let it sit untouched until it releases easily and has good grill marks, about 4 minutes.
Flip carefully, brush with half the sauce, and grill until the fish flakes easily, about 3 to 4 minutes more.
Break the salmon into large chunks.
Divide the warm rice between two bowls and top with the salmon, cucumber, and avocado.
Drizzle the remaining sauce over the bowls and finish with a scatter of sesame seeds.
Cook the white rice according to the package directions and keep it warm.
Heat the oven to 425°F and line a sheet pan with foil.
Whisk the tamari, honey, rice vinegar, and sesame oil together in a small bowl.
Pat the salmon dry, set it on the sheet pan, and brush with half the sauce.
Roast until the salmon is just about opaque at the edges, about 8 minutes.
Brush with the remaining sauce and roast until it flakes easily and looks glossy, about 3 to 4 more minutes.
Break the salmon into large chunks.
Divide the warm rice between two bowls, top with the salmon, cucumber, and avocado, and finish with a scatter of sesame seeds.

Cook the bacon in a skillet on the stovetop over medium heat until crisp, about 5 minutes, then lift it out onto a paper towel, leaving the fat in the pan — a slow cooker won't crisp bacon, so this step still needs the stovetop.
Add the onion and celery to the bacon fat and cook until softened, about 5 minutes.
Sprinkle the flour over the vegetables and stir constantly for 1 minute, then scrape everything into the slow cooker.
Stir the reserved clam juice from the cans and the bottled clam juice into the slow cooker, along with the potatoes and bay leaf.
Cover and cook on low until the potatoes are fork-tender, about 4 1/2 hours.
Stir in the heavy cream and milk during the last 20 minutes so they warm through gently — added any earlier, the dairy can break under hours of heat.
Add the chopped clams in the last 5 minutes and re-cover — clams turn rubbery fast, so they only need enough time to heat through, not to cook further.
Remove the bay leaf, season with salt and pepper, and ladle into bowls topped with the reserved crisp bacon.
Set the pressure cooker to sauté, cook the bacon until crisp, about 5 minutes, then lift it out onto a paper towel, leaving the fat behind.
Add the onion and celery to the fat and cook until softened, about 4 minutes.
Sprinkle in the flour and stir constantly for 1 minute, then pour in the reserved clam juice from the cans and the bottled clam juice, scraping up any browned bits.
Add the potatoes and bay leaf, lock the lid, and pressure cook on high for 5 minutes.
Quick release the pressure as soon as it's done — letting it sit would carry the potatoes past tender into mushy.
Switch back to sauté, stir in the heavy cream and milk, and warm through gently, about 3 minutes — do not let it boil hard.
Stir in the chopped clams and cook just 2 minutes on sauté — added at the very end so the pressure cycle never touches them and they stay tender.
Remove the bay leaf, season with salt and pepper, and ladle into bowls topped with the reserved crisp bacon.
Heat the olive oil in a skillet on the stovetop and cook the onion and carrots until softened, about 5 minutes — a quick sauté first builds more flavor than dropping everything in raw.
Add the garlic and stir until fragrant, about 30 seconds, then scrape everything into the slow cooker.
Add the vegetable broth and diced tomatoes to the slow cooker and season with salt and pepper.
Cover and cook on low until the vegetables are tender and the flavors have melded, about 5 hours (or high for 2 1/2 hours).
Stir in the tortellini during the last 20 minutes of cooking on high — fresh tortellini turns to mush if it simmers for hours, so it only goes in near the end.
Stir in the spinach in the last 5 minutes, just until wilted.
Ladle into bowls and top with parmesan cheese before serving.
Set the pressure cooker to sauté, heat the olive oil, and cook the onion and carrots until softened, about 4 minutes.
Add the garlic and stir until fragrant, about 30 seconds.
Pour in the vegetable broth and diced tomatoes, season with salt and pepper, and scrape up any browned bits.
Lock the lid and pressure cook on high for 3 minutes, then quick release — the vegetables just need to finish softening and the flavors to meld.

Switch back to sauté, stir in the tortellini, and simmer gently until tender and floating, about 4 minutes — pressure cooking fresh tortellini directly would turn it to paste, so it finishes in the open pot instead.
Stir in the spinach and cook just until wilted, about 1 minute.
Ladle into bowls and top with parmesan cheese before serving.
Set the pressure cooker to sauté, melt 2 tablespoons of the butter, and add the mushrooms in a single layer. Cook without stirring too much until deeply browned, about 6 minutes, then set aside.
Add 2 more tablespoons of butter to the pot along with the onion, cooking until soft, about 4 minutes.
Add the arborio rice and stir for about a minute until the edges of the grains look slightly translucent.
Pour in the white wine and stir until it's absorbed, about 1 minute.
Add all of the vegetable broth at once — pressure cooking means you don't need to add it gradually the way you would on the stovetop. Lock the lid and pressure cook on high for 6 minutes.
Quick release the pressure as soon as it's done — letting the rice sit under natural release would carry it past creamy into mushy.
Stir the browned mushrooms, remaining butter, and parmesan cheese back in, switching to sauté for a minute or two and stirring constantly until glossy and creamy — this mimics the stovetop finish.
Season with salt and pepper and serve immediately, while it's still loose and creamy.
Heat the oven to 375°F.

Melt 2 tablespoons of the butter in an oven-safe pot over medium-high heat on the stovetop and add the mushrooms in a single layer. Cook without stirring too much until deeply browned, about 6 minutes, then set aside.
Add 2 more tablespoons of butter to the same pot along with the onion, cooking until soft, about 4 minutes.
Add the arborio rice and stir for about a minute until the edges of the grains look slightly translucent.
Pour in the white wine and stir until it's absorbed, about 1 minute.

Pour in all of the vegetable broth at once, stir once, cover the pot tightly, and transfer it to the oven — the oven's steady heat means you don't have to stand and stir constantly like you would on the stovetop.
Bake until the rice is tender with just a little bite left and the broth is mostly absorbed, about 20 minutes.

Stir the browned mushrooms, remaining butter, and parmesan cheese in vigorously for about a minute until glossy and creamy — the vigorous stirring at the end releases the rice's starch and mimics a stovetop finish.
Season with salt and pepper and serve immediately, while it's still loose and creamy.
Preheat the air fryer to 370°F.
Stir the crushed tomatoes, garlic, salt, and pepper together in a small bowl.
Brush both flatbreads lightly with olive oil on one side.
Spread the tomato mixture evenly over the oiled side of each flatbread, leaving a small border.
Arrange the mozzarella slices over the top of each flatbread.

Place one flatbread at a time in the air fryer basket — most baskets only fit one, and crowding blocks the hot air that crisps the crust — and air fry until the cheese is melted and bubbling and the edges are golden, about 6 to 8 minutes.
Repeat with the second flatbread while the first stays warm.
Scatter the basil over both, slice, and serve hot.
Heat the olive oil in a skillet on the stovetop and cook the onion until softened, about 4 minutes.
Add the garlic, ginger, and curry powder, stirring until fragrant, about 1 minute, then scrape everything into the slow cooker.

Add the sweet potato, diced tomatoes, and only half the vegetable broth to the slow cooker — a slow cooker traps all its moisture instead of letting it evaporate, so the full amount would turn the curry watery.
Cover and cook on low until the sweet potato is fork-tender, about 6 1/2 hours (or high for 3 1/2 hours).
Stir in the peanut butter until fully melted into the sauce, then cover and cook 10 more minutes on high to let it meld.
Stir in the spinach, cover, and cook just until wilted, about 5 minutes.
Season with salt and pepper and serve warm.
Set the pressure cooker to sauté, heat the olive oil, and cook the onion until softened, about 4 minutes.
Add the garlic, ginger, and curry powder, stirring until fragrant, about 1 minute.
Add the sweet potato, diced tomatoes, and all of the vegetable broth — under pressure nothing evaporates, so unlike a slow cooker, the full amount is fine here.
Lock the lid and pressure cook on high for 8 minutes, then quick release.
Switch back to sauté, stir in the peanut butter until melted, and simmer uncovered for 3 minutes to thicken slightly.
Stir in the spinach and cook just until wilted, about 1 minute.
Season with salt and pepper and serve warm.
Whisk the soy sauce, cornstarch, and vegetable broth together in a small bowl until smooth; set aside.
Toss the broccoli and carrots with half the vegetable oil.

Preheat the air fryer to 400°F, then air fry the broccoli and carrots, shaking the basket halfway, until bright and starting to crisp at the edges, about 8 minutes — these take longest, so they go in first.
Toss the bell pepper and snap peas with the remaining oil, add them to the basket, and air fry until all the vegetables are bright and tender-crisp, about 4 more minutes.
Add the garlic and ginger to the basket for the final minute so they turn fragrant without burning — hot circulating air scorches minced garlic fast, so it goes in last, not first.
Meanwhile, warm the sauce in a small saucepan on the stovetop until it thickens and turns glossy, about 2 minutes — the air fryer can't reduce a sauce for you.
Toss the air-fried vegetables with the warm sauce until evenly coated.
Serve right away while the edges are still crisp - the sauce softens them as they sit.
